transcript: Hell's Kitchen might just be the best vocally performed musical in New York. This new musical which opened last night on Broadway is loosely based on the life of Alicia Keys and features over a dozen of her hits, all beautifully and theatrically arranged for this show. The story is fairly simple, revolving around a teenager named Ali living in Hell's Kitchen with her mother Jersey. It’s a story of teenage angst, self-discovery, love, loss, and music. Led by the stellar Maleah Joi Moon, Shoshana Bean, and Brandon Victor Dixon, the vocals alone are well worth the price of admission — I truly cannot overstate how good the vocals are in this show. Add in a beautiful production design, an incredible ensemble and supporting cast, and joyful choreography, this show, I would consider a must-see. Compared to the production at The Public that I saw in December, this version didn't feel very noticeably different to me, but the reviews do seem stronger now than they were then, so take with that what you will. I don't think the show is fully immune from some of the common issues with jukebox musicals, such as some rushed or forced plot points and underdeveloped relationships. But, and we can agree to disagree on this, I feel the heart of the show beats louder than any shortcomings and that the performances are just completely transcendent. I think the show does exactly what it sets out to do and that is to give the audience a great time, so Hell's Kitchen gets two thumbs up from me. With that, another Playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer gives a clear recommendation ('must-see', 'two thumbs up') with genuine enthusiasm for the vocals and performances, but tempers it with acknowledged shortcomings typical of jukebox musicals, including rushed plot points and underdeveloped relationships.
